evidence: FY2025 Form 10-K reports $8.342B total company sales and provides segment/geographic/customer-related disclosures but does not identify any single major external customer at or above the ASC 280 10% revenue threshold.

The latest FY2026 quarterly filing reviewed likewise contains revenue/customer-contract disclosures without identifying a single major external customer concentration; it reports remaining performance obligations and broad geographic revenue rather than a named dominant customer.
targets.inference: Because U.S. GAAP segment disclosure requires disclosure of a major customer when revenue from a single external customer is 10% or more of consolidated revenue, the absence of a named major customer in Rockwell's audited FY2025 major-customer disclosures is strong evidence that no single external customer crossed that threshold. Sensia's customer-base concentration is a reporting-unit/JV risk and should not be misclassified as a consolidated single-customer concentration.
targets.gateImpact: Removes the specific customer-concentration blocker for Chief review; retain normal end-market/channel concentration risk separately rather than holding promotion for a nonexistent disclosed >=10% consolidated customer.
